facts.title: fix: keep the reason in each flag, and bound the customer outcome by the facts
facts.description:
Follows #250 and #251, and the flag review of the ServiceDeskLite `v1.9.0` comparison runs they were built for.

Two commits, each on its own:

**`fix(faithfulness)`: keep the reason in each thorough-check flag**

- **Why:** #250 turned the verdict into `{ claim, pullRequest }`. With a field named only for the claim, the model returned only the claim: a smoke run came back with three quoted passages, no word on what was wrong with them, and 165 output tokens for two checks. A flag without its reason makes the reviewer redo the check, and it breaks `FaithfulnessFlag.Text`, documented as "what was flagged, and why".
- **What:** the verdict is `{ claim, reason, pullRequest }`, and the prompt asks for the quoted words and the reason. `CallValidity` joins them into the flag text as `"<claim>" - <reason>`.
- **One text field, not a new record field.** A rule-based flag already carries its reason in its text ("The number '3' is not supported..."), so a separate `reason` in the run record would be absent for half the flags. Record schema and docs stay as they are; the code now matches them.
- A claim without a reason is kept as the claim alone rather than dropped. Quotes the model put around the claim are taken off before ours go on, so the text does not read `"“...”"`.
- Prompt change: `thorough-system` snapshot and `promptHash` (`sha256:a642c294...`).

**`fix(prompting)`: bound the customer outcome by what the facts establish**

- **Why:** over three runs at the commit above (gpt-5.6-sol rendering and checking), 17 of 33 thorough-check flags quoted the customer outcome. The format requires an outcome on every entry and names "no longer have to" as its form, and the model filled it with a model instruction read as a guarantee (#221, #223 in all three runs), a behaviour promised beyond the part of the product it holds in, or a workaround no fact says the reader ever needed.
- **What:** an outcome carries the limit the facts name, as a condition the reader can place themselves in. A model instruction counts as an outcome stated as what the product tells the model, so the honest sentence no longer fails the mechanism test. Something the reader no longer has to do is named only when the facts say they had to do it; the fix rule allows "what they can now count on" instead, which it previously did not.
- **Two rules, nothing else.** The two example entries still close on "so you no longer have to...". They were left alone so the measurement below reads one change.
- Prompt change: `customer` snapshot and `promptHash` (`sha256:18467240...`).

**Verified on real runs:** `goldbarth/ServiceDeskLite` `v1.9.0 --since 675555a7`, 18 facts, `gpt-5.6-sol` rendering and checking through `openai-compatible`, thinking disabled. Three runs before the second commit, four after.

| per run | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| thorough-check flags | 11 | 6.25 |
| flags quoting the outcome formula | 5.7 | 1.75 |
| #221 / #223 flagged | 3 of 3 / 3 of 3 | 1 of 4 / 2 of 4 |
| #237, #244 (not touched by the change) | 3 of 3 / 3 of 3 | 3 of 4 / 2 of 4 |

- Every flag in all seven runs carries a reason and a pull request. OpenAI strict mode accepted the three-field schema.
- The untouched facts held, so the drop is not the check's own noise. #218 and #240 newly recur; their flags are mostly the check disputing wording the facts support, left for a change to the check itself.
- Whether bounding the outcome costs outcomes: C3 of chartula-evals, judged on two runs a side, 4 fails before and 8 after. Of the entries that moved, one plausibly follows from the change (the command palette lost "without leaving the keyboard"); one fails after with the same outcome sentence it passed with before, and one moved the other way. C3 is out of the judge's gate, so this is a direction. Recorded in chartula-evals `docs/measurements.md` (2026-09-24).
- Left open, not in this PR: a limit of scope still reads as general (#235, board vs. detail view), and "rely on" still promises permanence (#213, #244).

Tests: `ChatModelTests` (claim and reason joined, a claim without a reason kept, an already quoted claim not quoted twice), prompt snapshots for `thorough-system` and `customer`. Full suite 830 passing, build without warnings, `dotnet format` clean.

facts.title: feat(observability): record the range a run read in its run record
facts.description:
Follows #250, which introduced run record schema version 2, and #227 and #231.

- **Why:** a run over a wrong range looks like any other run of the same tag, with other facts and flags. The ServiceDeskLite `v1.9.0` comparison runs recorded 19 commits, while `v1.8.0..v1.9.0` holds 10 today, and nothing in those records says which range they read.
- **What:** `range: { start, from, fromCommit, toCommit }` next to `tag`. `start` is `previous-tag`, `since` or `whole-history`, named after the CLI's options. `from` is the ref as named or found.
- **Hashes, not only names:** a tag can be moved, and a `--since` ref such as a branch moves by itself. `git log <fromCommit>..<toCommit>` replays the range later. An annotated tag is peeled to its commit (`^{commit}`).
- **Resolved where the range is read:** `GitCliCommitReader` fills `CommitRange.FromCommit` and `ToCommit`, optional init properties so the test stubs stay as they are. `ToCommit` is the output of the `rev-parse --verify` the reader already runs; `fromCommit` costs one more `rev-parse`.
- **`start` is derived, not stored twice:** from the start the operator named and `CommitRange.From`, following `IReleaseCommitReader`'s contract: a named start wins, then the previous tag, then the whole history.
- Arrives in schema version 2 with #250. Absent in a version 1 record.
- `changelog.json` is unchanged.

**Verified end to end, no paid tokens:** binary from this branch against local Ollama (`gemma3:12b`) in a scratch clone of this repository:

```
$ chartula generate --no-publish --tag v0.1.0-preview.2 --since 616bbf5 --repo goldbarth/chartula
  "range": {
    "start": "since",
    "from": "616bbf5",
    "fromCommit": "616bbf50cae137a9f1f154908daa7a49740fed55",
    "toCommit": "ca35f082b088099ffc62deabc99111c95cbd874f"
  }

$ chartula generate --no-publish --tag v0.1.0-preview.2 --repo goldbarth/chartula
  "range": {
    "start": "previous-tag",
    "from": "v0.1.0-preview.1",
    "fromCommit": "8930f18d6438acd6a86e2da7b6d7f35f45e2e592",
    "toCommit": "ca35f082b088099ffc62deabc99111c95cbd874f"
  }
```

Every hash matches `git rev-parse` of its ref in the clone.

Tests: `GitCliCommitReaderTests` (both ends' commits kept, annotated tag peeled, whole history has no start commit, a named start's commit), `RunRecordPipelineTests` (range and named start reach the record), `RunRecordJsonSerializerTests` (the three starts, an unknown range left out). Full suite 828 passing, build without warnings, `dotnet format` clean.

facts.title: feat(faithfulness): name the pull request behind each flag
facts.description:
Follows the flag review of five ServiceDeskLite `v1.9.0` runs recorded with #227: 5 of 38 flags named a pull request anywhere in their text. The other 33 had to be traced to their fact by hand, and repeats across runs could only be grouped by how alike their wording was.

- **The check names the fact, code decides whether it is one.** The verdict schema is now `{ claim, pullRequest }` per claim. `ThoroughFaithfulnessChecker` keeps the number only when the fact base has that pull request, the same rule as for categories and links: the model never decides what is a fact.
- **One place for the number.** Each fact in the check's prompt opens on `[#n]`, and the prompt says to take the number from there only. Titles and descriptions mention issue numbers (#245's title ends in `(#243)`), which read like pull requests.
- **An unknown number is not dropped silently.** It leaves `pullRequest` but stays in the text as `(The check named #243, which is not a pull request of this release.)`, so the reviewer keeps the lead.
- **No number where there is no single fact:** rule-based flags (a token no fact contains), claims about the release as a whole such as the customer description, commit-based facts, and "could not be evaluated".
- **Existence, not correctness.** A number the release has is still the check's reading. `docs/run-record.md` says so.
- **Run record schema version 2.** `flags` becomes `[{ "text", "pullRequest"? }]`. Changing the element type is breaking, so the version is bumped rather than adding a parallel field that repeats every flag text. The record is local only, and nothing in chartula-evals reads its flags.
- Terminal and review output put the number first: `! #223: ...`.
- `IRunMetrics` stays string-based: the pipeline passes the flag texts, so the thorough-only count means what it did.
- Prompt change: `thorough-system` snapshot and `promptHash` updated (`sha256:abf516c2...`), so runs before and after differ in `promptHash`, as they should.

**Verified end to end, no paid tokens:** binary with this change against local Ollama (`gemma3:12b`, `factBase.depth: title-only`), `generate --no-publish --tag v0.1.0-preview.2` in a scratch clone of this repository:

```
--- Customer ---
  Flagged for review:
    ! #242: This expands the places where Chartula can be run, so you can now use it on a wider range of systems.
    ...
    ! #218: To restore access, please check your repository and token settings in the repository's settings.
```

- 24 of 24 flags named a pull request, all 24 in the fact base, none rewritten. In the run record each is `{ "text": ..., "pullRequest": 242 }`.
- The request schema of both real adapters, dumped from the wire test: `claim` string, `pullRequest` integer or null; OpenAI strict mode requires both.
- Whether a hosted model names the right fact as reliably is for the next comparison run.

Tests: `ChatModelTests` (claims with and without a number, a claim without text does not count), `ThoroughFaithfulnessCheckerTests` (a fact opens on its number, a known number is kept, an unknown one is dropped and noted), `ReviewPresentationTests` (a flag opens on its pull request), `RunRecordJsonSerializerTests` (flag objects, schema version 2). Full suite 821 passing, build without warnings, `dotnet format` clean.

facts.title: docs: rewrite comments for readability
facts.description:
Follows up on the comments across the codebase being hard to read on first pass.

- **Content kept, wording changed.** Most comments already explained the why. What made them hard to read was how they were written: the point came at the end of a chain of "because/so/which", things were circumscribed instead of named, pronouns had no clear referent, contrasts and negations stood in for a plain statement, several thoughts were packed into one sentence. Each rewrite puts the point first and names things by their code terms.
- **Why stays why.** No comment was shortened into a restatement of the code. Reasons, edge cases, numbers and issue references (`#94`, `#122`, ...) are kept. Statements that `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/architecture.md` or the ADRs point to (e.g. the `Labels` comment in `FactBaseBuilder`) keep their exact meaning.
- **Comments only.** No code, string, name or formatting change. The prompt texts in `ChangelogPromptBuilder.Prompts.cs` are string literals and untouched; the prompt snapshot and hash tests confirm it. The one code line in the diff is `ChangelogFormatter.BulletMarkers`, where only the trailing `// '•'` (a repeat of the literal) is removed.
- **Stale comments resolved:** `ReleaseChangeResolver` (title list "becomes configurable" - it did not), `CommitInfo` ("enriched by later issues"), `IChangelogModel` ("refined in the prompt-design issue"), `PipelineServiceCollectionExtensions` (named the wrong consumer of `IReleasePipeline`).
- **Scope:** 215 files - Core 87, Core.Tests 39, Cli 35, Cli.Tests 30, Infrastructure 12, Infrastructure.Tests 6, plus the workflows, installers, `check-install.sh` and `Chartula.Cli.csproj`. Excluded: `chartula.example.yaml` (its comments are user docs), fixtures, snapshots, `docs/`.
- One commit per folder, so each can be reviewed on its own.
- Found along the way, fixed separately: review mode on approved every text unseen (#247).

**Verification**

- `git diff -U0 main | grep -E '^[+-][^+-]' | grep -vE '^[+-]\s*(//|#|

facts.title: fix(cli): refuse review mode until an interactive reviewer exists
facts.description:
Follows #19.

- **The gap:** `docs/configuration.md` promised that `review.enabled: true` presents generated texts for human sign-off. The only registered `IReviewer` is `AutoApproveReviewer`, so with review mode on every text was approved without anyone seeing it. A setting that suggests a safeguard and does nothing is worse than no setting.
- **Refused at composition, not at the schema:** `AddChartulaReview` throws when `Enabled` is set, so `chartula.yaml` and `Chartula__Review__Enabled` are covered by the same check. It surfaces as `Configuration error: ...` with exit code 1, before any GitHub request or model call - the same path as the existing `llm.*` errors.
- **`enabled: false` stays valid:** the `review` key remains in `ChartulaYamlSchema`, so existing configs that spell out the default keep working.
- **Mechanism left in place:** `ReviewCoordinator`, `IReviewer` and the pipeline step are unchanged. The interactive reviewer that makes review mode usable is tracked in #249.
- Docs: the `review` section in `docs/configuration.md` and `chartula.example.yaml` say "not available yet". The `AutoApproveReviewer` and `ReviewServiceCollectionExtensions` comments no longer claim an interactive reviewer ships with the CLI.

**Reproduced before the fix:** `ReviewWiringTests.Review_mode_on_is_refused_naming_the_key` fails on main - `review: enabled: true` composes without error and registers the auto-approving reviewer.

**Verified after the fix**, binary from this branch (no tokens spent, the run stops at composition):

```
$ Chartula__Review__Enabled=true chartula preview --tag v0.1.0-preview.2
Configuration error: review.enabled is not available yet: no interactive reviewer exists, so every text would be approved unseen. Remove it or set it to false.
[exit code: 1]
```
Same message and exit code with `review:\n  enabled: true` in `chartula.yaml`.

Tests: `ReviewWiringTests` (on is refused naming `review.enabled`; off and absent register the coordinator). Full suite 816 passing, build without warnings, `dotnet format` clean.

facts.title: docs: add the changelog Chartula generated for 0.1.0-preview.2
facts.description:
Follows #139 and the `v0.1.0-preview.2` tag.

- `CHANGELOG.md` section for `0.1.0-preview.2` generated by Chartula and committed as written.
- Run: `generate --tag v0.1.0-preview.2`, provider `openai-compatible`, model `gpt-6-sol`, thinking `disabled`, thorough check on, binary `0.1.0-preview.2+ca35f08`. 24 pull requests, 23 facts, 69,876 tokens, 41 s. The same run wrote the draft release notes.
- Only the note above the sections was edited by hand. The old note said nothing was released and named one provider and model for the whole file. Both are no longer true, so it now lists the settings per release.
- `changelog.json` goes to chartula-evals (`test-runs/`), not here, as with #139.

**Verification**

- `toolVersion` in the run's `changelog.json` is `0.1.0-preview.2+ca35f082b088099ffc62deabc99111c95cbd874f`, the tagged commit.
- Thorough check: technical 0 flags, customer 2 (customer rendering is not in this file).

Tests: none, documentation only.
